edits.new: You can sow collard seeds right in the garden or start them indoors. For spring, start seeds about a month before planting out, and set plants in the garden a few weeks before your last frost, or just sow seeds once the soil can be worked. For a fall crop, sow in mid to late summer so it is ready before winter. Space full-size plants 12 to 24 inches apart. If you grow your own transplants, let them get used to the outdoors over a week before planting.
edits.reason: restates the moved in-row figure (UMD: 12-24 in)

edits.new: Collards can be direct sown or transplanted, and in the South direct sowing is the norm. For a spring crop, start seeds indoors about 4 to 5 weeks before set-out and transplant around 3 to 4 weeks before the last frost, or direct sow as soon as the soil is workable; collards tolerate frost. For a fall and winter crop, sow in mid to late summer so plants size up before cold, then harvest through fall and, in mild zones, winter. Harden transplants off over 7 to 10 days. Thin or set plants 12 to 24 inches apart for full-size plants.
edits.reason: restates the moved in-row figure (UMD: 12-24 in)

edits.new: Space plants about 12 to 24 inches apart for big plants, or closer together if you plan to cut them while young.
